reference_title: Design and Construction of Mechanically Stabilized Earth Walls and Reinforced Soil Slopes – Volume II

sections.title: Introduction
sections.body: Construction of MSE and RSS systems is relatively simple and rapid. The construction sequence consists of preparing the subgrade, placing and compacting backfill in normal lift operations, laying reinforcing layers, and installing facing elements (tensioning may also be required for RSS). Special skills or equipment are usually not required; locally available labor can be used. Table 11-1 provides an outline checklist for monitoring and inspecting MSE and RSS systems. Four main inspection areas: preconstruction reviews (Section 11.1); prefabricated materials inspection (Section 11.2); construction control (Section 11.3); performance monitoring programs (Section 11.4).
key_points: MSE/RSS construction is sequential: subgrade prep, backfill placement, reinforcement, facing
Locally available labor can be used; experienced crews provide higher production rates
Most material suppliers provide construction training
tables: Table 11-1: Outline of MSE/RSS Field Inspection Checklist Requirements
sections.applicability: All MSE wall and RSS construction projects

sections.title: Preconstruction Reviews
sections.body: Prior to structure erection, inspection personnel must be familiar with: plans and specifications, site conditions relevant to construction, material requirements, and construction sequences for the specific reinforcement system.
key_points: Inspector must review all four items before construction begins
Construction sequence is system-specific - must consult manufacturer's construction manual
sections.applicability: Pre-construction phase of all MSE/RSS projects

sections.title: Plans and Specifications Review
sections.body: Inspection personnel must review: specifications (material requirements, construction procedures, soil compaction, alignment tolerances, acceptance/rejection criteria); plans (construction sequence, corrosion protection, special placement for damage prevention, compaction restrictions, drainage details, utility construction, slope face construction details, contractor documents); material requirements and approval submittals; construction sequence for the reinforcement system. Table 11-2 provides a drawing review checklist. Table 11-3 provides a specification compliance checklist covering: Section 1 (General description, system acceptance, pre-activity meeting); Section 2 (Working drawings and design); Section 3 (Materials: precast elements, steel components, geosynthetics, fill materials, MBW units); Section 4 (Construction: leveling pad, drainage, wall erection, reinforcement, backfill); Section 5/6 (Measurement and payment). Table 11-3 also includes a Materials Receiving Inspection Checklist (Table 11-3b) with yes/no/NA format for checking: system acceptance, working drawings submittal status, materials certifications, contractor QC test frequency, QA test results compliance for reinforced soil, retained soil, and facing soil, and ancillary items verification.
key_points: Inspect specifications for: material requirements, compaction procedures, alignment tolerances, acceptance criteria
Inspect plans for: construction sequence, corrosion protection, drainage details, utility details
Review all submittals before construction begins
Table 11-2: drawing review checklist; Table 11-3: specification compliance checklist
tables: Table 11-3: Specification Compliance and Materials Receiving Inspection Checklist
sections.applicability: Preconstruction review phase

sections.title: Site Conditions and Drainage Requirements
sections.body: Inspector must review site conditions for drainage requirements and other construction considerations. Site drainage must be addressed to prevent water infiltration during and after construction. Drainage design must be reviewed relative to final site conditions.
key_points: Drainage requirements must be assessed for site-specific conditions
Surface water control during construction is critical to backfill quality
sections.applicability: Site assessment prior to construction

sections.title: Prefabricated Materials Inspection
sections.body: Material components should be examined at the casting yard (for precast elements) and on site. Material acceptance based on combination of material testing, certification, and visual observations. All delivered system components must be satisfactorily stored and handled to avoid damage.
key_points: Inspect both at casting yard and upon delivery to site
Accept/reject based on testing, certification, AND visual inspection
Material supplier's construction manual contains additional storage and handling guidance
sections.applicability: Material receiving inspection for all MSE/RSS components

sections.title: Precast Concrete Elements
sections.body: At casting yard: verify elements fabricated per agency specifications; verify clevis loop embeds, tie strips, and connection devices do NOT contact or attach to reinforcing steel; verify curing procedures. Reject panels for: insufficient compressive strength; mold defects; honeycombing; severe cracking, chipping, or spalling; significant color variation; out-of-tolerance dimensions; misalignment of connection devices. Maximum dimension tolerances for precast panels: overall dimensions +/- 1/2 inch (13 mm); connection device locations +/- 1 inch (25 mm); clevis loop embeds +/- 1/8 inch (3 mm) horizontal alignment; element squareness: max 1/2 inch (13 mm) difference between diagonals; smooth surface finish: 1/8 inch in 5 ft (2 mm in 1 m); textured surface finish: 5/16 inch in 5 ft (5 mm in 1 m). For drycast modular blocks: carefully check compressive strength and water absorption on lot basis. MBW tolerances: overall dimensions +/- 1/8 inch (3.2 mm); height +/- 1/16 inch (1.6 mm). Damaged elements may be repaired to Engineer's satisfaction.
key_points: Connection devices must NOT contact or attach to reinforcing steel (critical for corrosion isolation)
Panel tolerances: overall +/-13 mm; connections +/-25 mm; clevis +/-3 mm; squareness <13 mm
MBW tolerances: overall +/-3.2 mm, height +/-1.6 mm
Six deficiency types result in panel rejection including honeycombing, misaligned connections
figures: Figure 11-1: Casting yard for precast facing elements
sections.applicability: Precast concrete facing elements - segmental panels and MBW units

sections.title: Reinforcing Elements
sections.body: Reinforcing elements (strips, mesh, sheets) must arrive securely bundled or packaged to avoid damage. Many product types and configurations exist; inspector must verify proper identification and designation (AASHTO, ASTM, or agency specifications). Grid reinforcement: check wire diameter, length, width, and spacing of longitudinal and transverse members. Strip reinforcement: check length and thickness. Geosynthetics: weight in field to compare mass per unit area with manufacturer's ID value; send samples to lab for verification. Galvanization: min. 2 oz/ft2 (610 g/m2); epoxy coatings: min. 16 mils (0.41 mm); verify by certification or agency tests; check for defects. Geosynthetics: maintain UV protection during shipping; storage temperature max 140 F (60 C). Reject reinforcement at installation if defective, deteriorated, or damaged. Metal reinforcement must NOT contain bent, cut, or repaired (welded or bent-and-straightened) sections without design engineer approval. Geosynthetics must not contain tears, cuts, or punctures.
key_points: Color coding of roll ends helpful for complex configurations with multiple product styles
Galvanization minimum 2 oz/ft2 (610 g/m2); epoxy coatings minimum 16 mils (0.41 mm)
Geosynthetics: max storage temperature 140 F (60 C); protect from UV
No bent, cut, or welded metallic reinforcement without design engineer written approval
Geosynthetics with tears, cuts, or punctures must be replaced or repaired per design engineer
figures: Figure 11-2: Inspect reinforcing elements - variety of types and length marking on geogrid
sections.applicability: Metallic strips, welded wire mesh, and geosynthetic reinforcement receiving inspection

sections.title: Facing Joint Materials
sections.body: Bearing pads (HDPE, EPDM, PVC, neoprene), joint filler, and joint cover geotextiles must be properly packaged to minimize damage during unloading and handling. Polymer filler and geotextiles must be protected from sunlight during storage. Properties must be checked by laboratory tests from supplier or preapproval (qualified products list) for conformance with specification requirements. Samples should be sent to laboratory for verification testing. Incorrect material or incorrect placement can result in significant structure distress.
key_points: Wrong bearing pad material or incorrect placement can cause significant structure distress
EPDM, HDPE, PVC, and neoprene bearing pad types accepted
Geotextile joint covers must be protected from sunlight
sections.applicability: Panel joint materials inspection

sections.title: Reinforced Backfill
sections.body: Reinforced backfill is the key element in satisfactory performance. Both appropriate material and correct placement are important. Reinforced backfill specified for gradation, plasticity, soundness, and electrochemical requirements. Tests prior to and during construction for quality assurance basis. During construction: gradation and plasticity index testing at specified rate - typically 1 test per 2,000 yd3 (1,500 m3) on large projects, and whenever appearance/behavior of backfill changes noticeably.
key_points: Testing rate: typically 1 gradation + PI test per 2,000 yd3 (1,500 m3) on large projects
Additional testing required when fill appearance or behavior changes
Both pre-construction approval tests and construction QA tests required
sections.applicability: Reinforced fill QA during construction

sections.title: Construction Control
sections.body: Each construction step is controlled by method requirements and tolerances. Construction manuals for proprietary MSE systems must be obtained from contractor.
key_points: Proprietary system construction manual required on-site during construction
sections.applicability: All MSE/RSS construction phases

sections.title: Leveling Pad
sections.body: Concrete leveling pad must have minimum dimensions per plans and specifications - typically 6 inches (150 mm) thick by panel width plus 8 inches (200 mm) wide. Concrete compressive strength must meet minimum spec requirements. Curing of CIP pads: typically minimum 12 to 24 hours before placing facing units. Vertical tolerance: +/- 1/8 inch (3 mm) to design elevation. Improperly placed leveling pad leads to misalignment, cracking, and spalling of facing units. Full-height precast panels require larger leveling pad for alignment and temporary foundation support. Gravel pads may be used for modular block walls in landscaping applications.
key_points: Typical dimensions: 6 in (150 mm) thick; width = panel + 8 in (200 mm)
Vertical tolerance: +/-1/8 inch (3 mm) to design elevation
Cure minimum 12-24 hours before placing facing units
Start adjacent to any existing structure and proceed toward open end
figures: Figure 11-3: Concrete leveling pad installation sequence
sections.applicability: Leveling pad construction and inspection

sections.title: Erection of Facing Elements
sections.body: Precast facing panels set at slight backward batter (toward reinforced fill) to assure correct final vertical alignment after backfill placement. Minor outward movement is expected and cannot be avoided. Typical backward batter: 1/2 inch in 4 ft (20 mm per meter) of panel height for steel reinforcements. Modular block units typically stacked with 1/2 to 1 inch offset. Full-height precast panels are more susceptible to cracking and misalignment than segmental panels - require additional bracing and larger face panel batter. Construction sequence for first row: start adjacent to existing structure and proceed toward open end. Facing elements on leveling pad directly; horizontal joint material or shims generally not permitted between first course and leveling pad (unless specifications allow with specific requirements). Temporary wood wedges may be used to set batter but must be removed during subsequent construction. Wooden wedges remain until third panel layer is set, then removed sequentially. Geotextile filter over openings at leveling pad, extending min. 6 inches beyond edges; openings > 1 inch filled with concrete or concurrently backfilled on both sides.
key_points: Batter for segmental panels: 20 mm per meter of panel height with steel reinforcement
MBW offset: 1/2 to 1 inch (12-25 mm) per course for horizontal movement accommodation
Temporary wood wedges must be removed - bottom row removed when third layer placed
Geotextile filter over all gaps at leveling pad; large gaps (>1 in) filled with concrete

Figure 11-5: Full height facing panels - special alignment care
Figure 11-6: Setting the first row of precast facing elements
sections.applicability: Facing element erection for segmental precast panels and MBW units

sections.title: Reinforced Fill Placement and Compaction
sections.body: Moisture and density control is imperative. Placement moisture: within 2% dry of optimum (wopt - 2% to wopt). For free-draining fill with < 5% passing No. 200: moisture within +/-3% of optimum. Density requirements: walls and slopes = 95% T-99 (or 90% T-180); abutments/structural foundations = 100% T-99 (or 95% T-180). For > 30% retained on 3/4-inch sieve: procedural specification preferred (typically 4-5 passes vibratory roller). Backfill placement: dump onto rear and middle of reinforcements and blade toward/away from face; compaction equipment must NOT be in direct contact with reinforcements; compact soil up to 2 inches above reinforcement connection elevation before placing next reinforcement layer. Within 3-foot (1 m) zone from face: small single or double drum walk-behind vibratory rollers or vibratory plate compactors; 4 passes lightweight equipment for quality control by method specification; do not lag more than one lift behind rest of structure. Away from face: large smooth-drum vibratory rollers; no sheepsfoot or grid rollers (may damage reinforcement); for uniform medium to fine sands (>60% passing No. 40): smooth-drum static or lightweight vibratory roller to prevent loosening. Minimum testing frequency: 1 density test per lift per 150 ft (45 m) of wall length. End of each day: grade fill away from face and lightly compact surface to reduce precipitation infiltration. Next day: scarify backfill surface (especially fines) to prevent shear planes between lifts.
key_points: Placement moisture: 2% dry of optimum (wopt - 2% to wopt); free-draining fill: +/-3% of wopt
Density: walls = 95% T-99; abutments = 100% T-99
3 ft (1 m) zone from face: light vibratory equipment only; 4 passes minimum by method spec
Equipment must never be in direct contact with reinforcements
Testing: 1 density test per lift per 150 ft (45 m) of wall
End of day: grade fill away from face; next day: scarify before placing new lift
figures: Figure 11-8: Compaction equipment - large equipment away from face; lightweight within 3 ft
sections.applicability: Reinforced fill placement and compaction for MSE walls and RSS

sections.title: Placement of Reinforcing Elements
sections.body: Reinforcing elements must be installed in strict compliance with spacing and length requirements. Reinforcements placed perpendicular to back of facing panel (perpendicular to wall face). Skewing may be permissible at abutments and curved walls; must not exceed specification limits; overlapping layers separated by minimum 3-inch (75 mm) fill. Curved walls: different procedures for convex and concave curves; joints further closed or opened by nominal facing movements. Around deep foundations: drive piles before face construction OR use hollow sleeves during fill erection (preferred); predrilling through reinforced fill is risky and must be avoided. Connections: manufacturer-specific; for flexible reinforcements (geotextiles, geogrids) - pretension to remove slack, then maintain by staking or fill placement.
key_points: Reinforcement perpendicular to wall face; skew allowed in special cases only (max per spec)
Overlapping reinforcements: minimum 75 mm (3 in) vertical separation
Deep foundations: hollow sleeves preferred over predrilling through reinforced fill
Flexible reinforcement connections must be pretensioned to remove all slack
sections.applicability: Reinforcement placement for all MSE/RSS types

sections.title: Placement of Subsequent Facing Courses and Alignment Tolerances
sections.body: Segmental panels: only set at grade; no panel placed on top of one not completely backfilled. Alignment tolerances: adjacent facing panel joint gaps: 3/4 inch +/- 1/4 inch (19 mm +/- 6 mm); precast face panel: 1/2 inch per 10 ft (6 mm per m) horizontal and vertical; wrapped face walls/slopes (welded wire or geosynthetic): 2 inches per 10 ft (15 mm per m) horizontal and vertical; wrapped face overall vertical: 1 inch per 10 ft (8 mm per m); wrapped face bulging: 1 to 2 inches (25 to 50 mm) maximum; reinforcement placement elevations: within 1 inch (25 mm) of connection elevation. Bearing pads (HDPE, EPDM, PVC, neoprene) used on horizontal joints; thickness based on anticipated short-term and long-term settlement. Filter geotextiles on joints prevent erosion while allowing water passage. Out-of-tolerance facing: do NOT push or pull into place (damages panels and reinforcements); must remove fill and reinforcements and reset panels. Table 11-4 lists out-of-tolerance conditions and possible causes.
key_points: Precast panel alignment: max 6 mm per meter deviation in horizontal and vertical
Wrapped face alignment: max 15 mm per meter; max bulging 25-50 mm
Never push or pull out-of-tolerance panels - must remove fill and reset
Post-erection deformations may indicate foundation, drainage, or retained soil problems
figures: Figure 11-10: Geotextile joint cover and EPDM bearing pads

tables.title: Out-of-Tolerance Conditions and Possible Causes
tables.content: Distress in wall: soft/wet foundation or poor fill compaction. First panel course difficult to set: leveling pad not level. Leaning out: insufficient batter, oversized equipment within 3 ft, wet of optimum moisture, fill pushed against face before compaction, excess compaction of fine sands. Leaning in: excessive batter, inadequate compaction, bearing capacity failure. Bulging: see causes of leaning out; saturated backfill. Panels not fitting: differential settlement, panels out of tolerance. Large adjacent panel movement: non-uniform fill or compaction.

sections.title: Performance Monitoring Programs
sections.body: Since MSE and RSS technologies are well-established, monitoring programs should be limited to cases where: new features or materials have been incorporated; substantial post-construction settlements are anticipated or construction rates require control; degradation/corrosion rates of reinforcements are to be monitored; or for asset management. Corrosion/degradation monitoring outlined in companion Corrosion/Degradation document (FHWA NHI-09-087).
key_points: Routine MSE/RSS construction typically does not require extensive monitoring
Monitoring warranted for: new materials/features, large expected settlements, corrosion monitoring, asset management
Companion document FHWA NHI-09-087 covers corrosion/degradation monitoring
sections.applicability: Performance monitoring program planning

sections.title: Purpose of Monitoring Program
sections.body: First step: define purpose of measurements. Every instrument must be selected to assist in answering a specific question. If there is no question, there should be no instrumentation. Identify significant parameters of interest and secondary parameters that may influence primary parameters. Important parameters: horizontal movements of face (MSEW); vertical movements of overall structure surface; local movements or deterioration of facing elements; drainage behavior of backfill; performance of structure supported by reinforced soil (approach slabs, footings); horizontal movements within structure; vertical movements within structure; lateral earth pressure at back of facing; vertical stress distribution at base; stresses in reinforcement (magnitude and location of maximum); stress distribution due to surcharge; relationship between settlement and stress-strain; stress relaxation in reinforcement over time; aging/corrosion condition of reinforcement; pore pressure response below structure; temperature; rainfall; barometric pressure.
key_points: No instrument without a specific question to answer
Foundation settlement will affect stress distribution within the structure
Stiffness of reinforcement affects anticipated lateral stress conditions in retained soil
sections.applicability: Monitoring program planning phase

sections.title: Limited Monitoring Program
sections.body: Limited observations that should be performed on practically all structures: horizontal and vertical movements of face (MSEW); vertical movements of surface of overall structure; local movements or deterioration of facing elements; performance of structure supported by reinforced soil (approach slabs, footings). Survey monitoring with measuring points on facing elements or pavement/retained soil surface. Permanent benchmarks required for vertical control; one horizontal control station at each end of structure. Maximum lateral movement during construction: H/250 for inextensible reinforcement; H/75 for extensible reinforcement. Tilting due to differential lateral movement: < 1/4 inch per 5 ft (4 mm per m) of wall height for either system. Post-construction horizontal movements anticipated to be very small.
key_points: Maximum construction lateral movement: H/250 inextensible (steel); H/75 extensible (geosynthetic)
Tilting: < 4 mm per meter of wall height for both systems
Foundation settlement must be estimated and measured during/after construction
Permanent benchmarks and horizontal control stations at each end required
sections.applicability: Minimum monitoring for all MSE/RSS structures

sections.title: Comprehensive Monitoring Program
sections.body: Involves monitoring of surface AND internal behavior of the reinforced soil. Predetermination of warning levels required whenever measurements used for construction control, safety, or less conservative designs; action plan must be established. Comprehensive program may include: deflection monitoring to establish gross performance and locate/quantify local distress; structural performance monitoring for tensile stress levels in reinforcement or connection stresses, and degradation rates; pullout resistance proof testing to establish pullout resistance vs. depth and elongation. Possible instruments per Table 11-6.
key_points: Warning levels must be predetermined before monitoring for safety or design control
Action plan required including notification and design alternatives
Three monitoring categories: deflection, structural performance, pullout resistance

tables.title: Possible Instruments for Monitoring Reinforced Soil Structures
tables.content: Horizontal face movements: visual, surveying, horizontal control stations, tiltmeters. Vertical movements: visual, surveying, benchmarks, tiltmeters. Facing deterioration: visual, crack gauges. Drainage behavior: visual at outflows, open standpipe piezometers. Horizontal movements within structure: surveying, horizontal control stations, probe extensometers, inclinometers, tiltmeters. Vertical movements within structure: surveying, benchmarks, probe extensometers, horizontal inclinometers, liquid level gauges. Lateral earth pressure at face: earth pressure cells, strain gauges at connections, load cells. Base stress distribution: earth pressure cells. Reinforcement stress: resistance strain gauges, induction coil gauges, hydraulic strain gauges, vibrating wire strain gauges, multiple telltales. Pore pressure: open standpipe piezometers, pneumatic piezometers, vibrating wire piezometers. Temperature: thermocouples, thermistors, resistance temperature devices, frost gauges. Rainfall: rainfall gauge. Barometric pressure: barometric pressure gauge.

sections.applicability: Comprehensive monitoring for new systems, critical structures, or research

sections.title: Program Implementation
sections.body: Instrument location selection involves three steps: (1) identify sections with unique design features (high surcharge, maximum stress) and locate instrumentation; (2) identify cross-sections with predicted behavior representative of whole structure as primary instrumented sections - at least two primary sections; (3) install simple instrumentation at secondary instrumented sections as indices of comparative behavior. Access to instrumentation locations and construction survivability are critical considerations. Strain gauges midway between adjacent extensometer attachment points for cross-checking. Step-by-step installation procedures prepared well in advance. Reference: FHWA RD 89-043 (Christopher et al. 1989) and FHWA HI-98-034 (Dunnicliff 1998).
key_points: Minimum two primary instrumented sections for comprehensive programs
Secondary sections verify primary sections are representative
Cross-check instruments: strain gauges midway between extensometer attachment points
Consult construction contractor on installation schedule compatibility
sections.applicability: Instrumentation layout and installation planning

sections.title: Data Interpretation
sections.body: Monitoring programs have failed because data was never used. Clear purpose guides method of data interpretation. Communication channels between design and field personnel must remain open. Early data interpretation: evaluate data correctness and detect changes requiring immediate action. Subsequent interpretation: correlate instrument readings with other factors (cause and effect), study deviation of readings from predicted behavior. After each data set: prepare interim monitoring report summarizing: updated summary plots, commentary on significant changes since last report, probable causes, and recommended action. Final report documents key aspects of monitoring program, supports remedial actions, and forms bank of experience.
key_points: Data must be used or monitoring program is wasted - purpose drives interpretation method
Interim monitoring reports required after each data collection event
Each report must include: summary plots, commentary on changes, probable causes, recommended action
Final report distributed to owner and design consultant for lessons learned
sections.applicability: All performance monitoring programs
